In 1533, he passed away at the age of unknown years, leaving behind a legacy that has been largely overshadowed by his contemporaries.


Ciocchi del Monte was instrumental in the canonization process of Saint Pius V, who would go on to become Pope in 1566. His involvement with the Catholic Church also led to his participation in several high-profile conclaves, including the one that elected Pope Gregory XIII in 1572.


The Italian city-state of Bologna played a crucial role in Ciocchi del Monte's life and career, as he served as the bishop of Bologna from 1519 until his death. His tenure was marked by significant religious reforms and efforts to strengthen ties between the Catholic Church and the local population.


In the aftermath of his passing, Ciocchi del Monte's legacy has been largely relegated to the footnotes of history, overshadowed by more prominent figures of the time.
